purpose: Document-level recency metadata for the 'recency' stale-fact condition. Attached to each excerpt label in the prompt; retrieval is unchanged.
note: One condition is run: recency_git. recency_content is documented but not run. Two conditions (Roy, 2026-11-06). Attached to excerpt labels only; retrieval unchanged. CORRECTIONS.md never receives a date (corrections_doc and recency are separate conditions, never combined).

recency_git.derivation: git log -1 --format=%cI 9bfc7b1 -- <file> in ~/Downloads/NFL (the frozen snapshot commit). This is the date an automated pipeline would get.
recency_git.known_property_before_running: README, PART1_DETAIL and CONTEXT share ONE commit timestamp, because the repo was published in two days. The instruction therefore cannot separate CONTEXT.md (most old sites) from README/PART1_DETAIL, and it ranks TIER2A_RESULTS.md, which holds SF9's corrected bottom line, as the OLDEST file. This is a property of VCS-derived recency, stated before any answer exists, not a defect to fix after.

recency_content.derivation: Mechanical (Roy): per-file content date = the newest `git blame --line-porcelain` committer-time at 9bfc7b1 among the lines in that file that hold a CURRENT value in eval/stale_facts.json (current_sites). A file with no current-value line (REPRODUCING.md) has no defined content date and gets its recency_git date. That fallback is a rule, not a judgement.
recency_content.known_property_before_running: DOES NOT FULFIL ITS PURPOSE. Blame dates are also publication dates: the repo's history starts with the 2026-11-02 import, so the real content dates (runs of 2026-09/10) are not in git. CONTEXT.md ties PART1_DETAIL.md for NEWEST, README.md is older than both, and TIER2A_RESULTS.md is still oldest. These dates carry no more information than recency_git, and rank the main stale-value file first. Raised with Roy before the freeze.
recency_content.status: NOT RUN (Roy, 2026-11-06). The derivation was attempted and gives no information beyond recency_git; kept here as the record of the failed attempt.
